body:
CHIEF: THE MOST IMPORTANT NUMBER OF THE DAY, and it is the direct answer to the owner's question.
m1 stopped chasing a blocked ablation and asked a better question that needed no reserved file.

DOES THE SHIPPED LIBRARY ALIGN WOG OUT OF THE BOX? Defaults throughout -- DefaultLocalCostModel,
default weights and externalFloor, lexicalJaccard, NO synonym table, NO canonicalisation, public
API only.

  OF THE EIGHT PARAPHRASES DECLARING A SOURCE TARGET, ONE IS HIT AT TOP-5. NONE AT TOP-1 OR TOP-3.

AND IT DOES NOT PICK THE WRONG NODE -- IT DECLINES TO ANCHOR. ext:Intrusion is the top state for
seven of ten, at 0.37 to 0.85 of the row. Summary 0.812 with 0.073 source mass; Blended 0.853 with
0.025.

THAT DISTINCTION IS THE WHOLE PROJECT WORKING. A model that confidently anchored the wrong event
would be the Article I failure -- a measurement we could not make, published as one we made. This
one abstains. Every rule we have written about Missing, Ineligible, refusing to impute, and not
scoring absence as agreement is what produces that abstention. The library is behaving exactly as
designed while being unable to do the task.

THE ENCOURAGING HALF, which m1 put next to it so the number is not read alone: THE EXTERNAL
CLASSIFICATION WORKS UNAIDED. ExternalAssociation -> ext:Association at 0.874. The Inference
paraphrase -> SourceConsistentInference at 0.744. Those routes come from DISCOURSE FUNCTION via the
segmenter, not from semantic matching, and they need none of the hand-authored resources. So the
part of the model that says "this came from outside the story" is functioning. The part that says
"this is THAT event" is not.

AND m1 CORRECTED ITS OWN METRIC BEFORE POSTING, against its own headline. Its first pass said 0/10.
ExternalAssociation declares Vector.empty targets -- it is SUPPOSED to be external, and it worked
correctly -- so counting it a miss was unfair to the library. Eight, not ten. That is the fourth
time today m1 has weakened its own finding with a measurement.

THIS IS NOT A DEFECT REPORT, AND I VERIFIED WHY. WarOfTheGhostsAlignmentSuite:199-201 says it in
the code's own words:

  "Lexical-only calibration: with no graded semantics the propositional and entity terms are mostly
   uninformative noise from the baseline segmenter, so they are down-weighted and the external
   floor is raised. TODO(M5): replace with calibrated defaults once embeddings and provider charts
   exist; THESE NUMBERS ARE PROVISIONAL, NOT SCIENTIFIC."

The defaults were never claimed to work. What nobody had done is say HOW FAR OFF THEY ARE, and now
we know: eight of eight, declining rather than guessing.

WHAT THIS MEANS FOR THE OWNER'S QUESTION -- code red or patient infrastructure. It is the strongest
evidence yet for the answer I gave: NOT a code red, and the allocation was wrong. The abstention
proves the correctness scaffolding does what it was built for. The one-of-eight proves the semantic
channel is the actual product and it is unbuilt -- and the code has said so, in a TODO, the whole
time. Both halves needed to be true at once and now both are measured.

Filing nothing. This is not a bug and there is no bead to open. It is the honest baseline we did
not have this morning, and it belongs in the release notes and in any paper before it belongs in a
tracker.
